column1: ## Part 7: the whole pipeline (part 6) WITH THE CLEAN-UP, second captures (round4/variants/): part 6's stored and repaired
## templates (llm-templates-learn-repaired over llm-templates-learn) plus the 7 new first-contact ones, with a key (repair
## where a template meets a new kind of line; llm_round.sh --round4 --inputs round4/variants --templates ... --learn), 2026-10-27.
## The 64 inputs whose output changed were rated again, blind (rerated=yes); the other 43 keep part 6's rating.

column7: note

All three package lists (13 rows with section names), the 0/7/0/23 summary line and all 14 Inst/Conf actions with version, archives and arch in the right columns are kept, and the simulation preamble is preserved verbatim in notes.

Both summary counts, all 7 counterexample conflicts (type, tokens, flag, example) and all 27 derivation steps with conflict id, derivation kind, depth, rule and production are kept in stable columns; the constant 'warning' word is not a column but the -W flag retains it.

Every section survives as its own table: 4 conflicts, 14 grammar rules, 10 terminals, 5 nonterminals with on-left/on-right, 8 state items with lookaheads and 23 state actions (bracketed reductions marked disabled), with only the redundant nonterminal name after reduce rule numbers left out.

All values survive (3 failed tests with durations, matcher messages, expected/received pairs, file:line:col locations, the 5/1/3/8 counts and the 9-test run line), but each failure diagnostic is split across four tables joined only by row order, and assertion_values has two rows per failure with no test key.

The Environment key/values with their Ruby/RubyGems/OpenSSL/Tools grouping, the build metadata and the Gemfile lines are right, but the Bundler settings values (Set via BUNDLE_*: ...) and all Gemfile.lock entries sit in the Key column with Value empty, and puma's nested nio4r (~> 2.0) dependency is flattened to look like a sibling spec.

All 45 AST nodes are kept with depth, parent address, node kind, address, range, location and details, but the second FunctionDecl (prev 0x5610f3a2c1e8) has empty Range and Location columns, with its range <inventory.c:30:1, line:36:1> and location line:30:6 left inside Details.

All 77 timer rows from the seven sections (Total rows included) carry name and paired time/percent values under the right User/System/User+System/Wall columns (checked row by row), and the six Total Execution Time lines go to their own table.

Every section is kept: 28 AST layout fields with offsets including bit ranges and nesting depth, 4 sizeof/align rows, 4 RecordDecls, 16 FieldDecls with bit widths, 4 LLVM types and 3 CGBitFieldInfo rows; only the bitfield width sub-nodes are folded into a BitWidth column.

All 42 trace lines (file, line, command, args, stray trailing text) and 10 status messages are filed correctly, but the one CMake Warning record is split across two datasets (level/file/line/command in diagnostics, its text in diagnostic_messages) with no key joining them, and the interleaving of status messages with trace lines is lost.

Version and date, all 11 global options split into short/long/description, all 39 commands (namespaced test:* included) with bracketed aliases in their own column, and the test namespace are kept; only the ASCII-art banner is dropped.
Legend (3 color/meaning rows) and all 98 warning flags filed in two datasets, each flag with depth and parent exactly matching the indentation tree, nothing lost.

All 24 TERM patterns, 18 file-type colours with comments and 23 extension colours are correct, but LINK's two-line comment is split: the row stops at 'instead of a' and the continuation ('numerical value, the color is as for the file pointed to.)') went to notes instead.
The device summary (all 8 fields) is one row and all 7 histogram buckets have range start/end, free extents, free blocks and percent in the right columns, with nothing lost.

All 36 pattern elements land as named columns in one row and the 45 charset pages split cleanly into page+word0..7 (header line kept in notes), but every value's binding/type suffix ((s)/(w) strong vs weak binding, (i)/(f) type) is stripped, so which elements are weakly bound (fullname, antialias, hintstyle, index, rgba, capability, lcdfilter) is lost.

Source header, all 4 function summaries, all 37 annotated source lines (count, line, code), all 18 branch records and 4 call records are filed in named columns, each tied to its function and source line, with fallthrough/never-executed notes kept.

All 7 function blocks and 3 file blocks land one per row with percent and total for lines/branches/taken/calls plus the created .gcov name under the right columns (stdio2.h's 'No branches' as empty branch fields), and the closing 80.95%-of-42 total is kept as its own summary row.
The 8 top-level fields file as one named row and all 49 attributes as namespace/attribute/value rows with values intact (multi-value icons kept whole); only the 'attributes:' heading goes to notes.

WORK, modinfo, 16 commands (env, args and '# internal' note split out) and all 69 packagefile entries are present, but the three 'cat >…importcfg << EOF' heredoc commands are left only as skipped notes and the packagefile rows carry no column saying which importcfg (b002/importcfg 3, b001/importcfg 7, b001/importcfg.link 59) they belong to, so that grouping is lost.

Package name, import path and package doc (with example) form one row, and all 20 declarations land one per row with section/kind/receiver/name, full declaration and their multi-line doc joined; only the TYPES heading goes to notes.

Read as YAML into a single 107-column row with each linter name as a column and its description as the value, so the 108 linter records are not one per row, the Enabled (19) vs Disabled (89) sections are merged with no way to tell which is which, 'wsl [deprecated]' is dropped entirely, and the [fast, auto-fix] tags stay glued to the descriptions.

All 12 issues land one per row with file/line/col/linter/message/source-line in named columns, and the '12 issues' total and the 6-row per-linter breakdown are kept; only the caret pointer lines (decoration, already captured as col) are dropped.

The flat profile (6 rows, all 8 named columns) and the 7 primary call-graph entries are exact, but the 12 caller/callee lines carry no link to their primary entry and no caller-vs-callee role, so the call graph's edges cannot be reconstructed, and the function_index dataset is 3 empty rows (index/name pairs lost there, though recoverable from the entries table).
Source file, the entry name/alias/description and all 101 capabilities (6 boolean, 4 numeric, 91 string) are kept one per row with name, type and value correct, escape strings intact.

All 90 log lines are accounted for: 16 init settings as one named record, 5 pauses with heap before/after/capacity/duration, 20 phases, 16 region transitions, 5 cpu lines and 28 remaining events each with uptime/level/tags/GC id; only the init lines' 0.004s/0.006s timestamps are folded away, which loses nothing substantive.

Class header, all 8 members with descriptors, all 59 bytecode instructions (offset/opcode/operands/comment, keyed by member), 9 LineNumberTable and 9 LocalVariableTable rows are filed under correct names; only Code:/table headings go to notes (the input itself is truncated at the last LineNumberTable).

Every section survives with named columns: total usage, 3 usage rows (all values and percentages split), virtual space, 45 chunk freelist rows ((none) as count 0) plus 3 totals, waste breakdown, header pool, 13 internal statistics and 10 settings; the PID and section headings sit in notes.

All 12 events are kept, 6 GCHeapMemoryPoolUsage and 6 ThreadStart rows with every field (thread names split from javaThreadIds), and the 14 stack frames go to a linked table keyed by event number with method and line; only the '...' elision marker is dropped.
Recording header (version, chunks, start, duration) is one record and all 46 event types are rows under Event_Type/Count/Size_(bytes), values exact; only the rule line is dropped.

PID, JVM version, GC and thread count, all 12 heap configuration settings, and the 4 heap-usage spaces (regions/capacity/used/free/% used) are filed under named columns; the dropped parenthetical MB figures in usage are exact conversions of the bytes kept, and the bare 'G1 Young Generation:' grouping label is the only line not carried.
All 19 plugins are one row each with option, argument and the full multi-line description joined; the trailing pattern-list footnote is kept verbatim (line by line) in notes.

Timestamp/JVM, SMR list header and its 18 addresses, all 28 threads with every header field split into named columns (VM-internal threads blank where they have no #/prio), all 89 stack/lock/info lines keyed to their thread, and the JNI refs summary all survive.
All 18 CPUs and 46 features land one per row as name/description in separate datasets, and the header lines and the two trailing usage lines are kept verbatim in notes, so nothing is lost.

Every section (executable, breakpoint, process events, threads, 7 frames, source listing, 3 frame variables, 5 images) is filed with correct columns and the commands kept in notes, but the two printed structs (p *it and p *it->next) are flattened into one 8-row member/value list with no column saying which object or type each member belongs to, so each struct record is split across rows and the grouping survives only by row order.

File/format, the compile-unit header (all 9 fields), all 23 DIEs with offset/depth/tag and all 106 attributes keyed by DIE offset with name and value are filed intact, with only the .debug_info heading and NULL terminators left to notes.

Summary metrics, both legends, the 6-row instruction-info table (MayLoad/MayStore stars under the right flags) and both resource-pressure tables with [0]..[13] resolved to resource names and every value in its column all survive, with only section headings in notes.

All three parts survive with real field names: the file summary, the whole ElfHeader (Ident sub-block flattened in) as one row, and all 7 sections including the truncated last one, one section per row with flag names collected into a FlagsNames column; only the per-flag hex constants (redundant with the Flags total) are dropped.

All 9 build steps (step/total/description), the warning as one row with file/line/column/severity/message/flag, the '1 warning generated' count, all 8 metrics rows under their real headers and the hash-load figures (0.69, 373 entries, 541 buckets) are filed, with the directory banner and source excerpt kept in notes; only the 'path->node' label and the caret line are not carried.

All 19 GC events land one per row with pid, isolate, time, type, heap before/after and committed sizes, pause, mu values and reason in stable columns (the Mark-Compact incremental-marking details in their own columns), and the two interleaved 'kept N' program lines are preserved verbatim in notes.

All 59 ops are filed one per row with sequence, class, op with arguments, flags and next pointer correctly split (and 'syntax OK' kept in notes), but the indentation that encodes the op tree's parent/child nesting is dropped with no depth column, so the tree structure of the optree is lost.

All 18 measurements across the five test sections land one per row with the section title, method, ops/sec and usecs/op (n/a and n/a* kept), and the preamble ('1 second per test', O_DIRECT note), parenthetical explanations and the * footnote are preserved verbatim in notes.

All 12 histogram buckets are filed with their real headers (the '< us' bound named 'us') and correct percent and count values, the per-loop overhead 21.87 ns is a summary field, and the '2 seconds' test line and histogram title are kept verbatim in notes.

The class header, all five section counts, both constants with values, all 7 properties, all 11 methods (section, origin, modifiers, return type and Return/Tentative return kind) and all 8 parameters keyed by method with position, required/optional, type, name and default are filed, with the per-method parameter counts kept in notes.
All 8 diagnostics are one row each with severity, message, line (including '-') and file correctly split out, and the closing '4 pod syntax errors' count is kept as a summary row.

All 80 headerless tab-separated rows are kept byte-for-byte, under accurate pg_settings names (name, context, category, vartype, boot_val, min_val, max_val, short_desc, extra_desc), with empty fields kept in place.

All 32 fields of the prtstat record land as one wide row with real names (section prefixes kept for the minor/major and user/system/guest/blkio sub-columns, units and '(non RT)' retained), and the section headings are only grouping decoration recorded as notes.

Every section survives: module name/summary/reference URL/file in one row, the four functions one row each with name, signature and full docstring (the pattern list folded into the doc text, nothing lost), the __all__ data entry, and the MODULE REFERENCE and DESCRIPTION prose kept whole per section.

All 17 formatters land one per row with their aliases, two-line description joined into one cell and the '(filenames ...)' suffix split into its own filenames column, and the version/copyright banner is kept verbatim in the notes dataset.

Every section survives in its own dataset: session header (platform/versions/rootdir/plugins/collected 11), the progress line, both failures plus the netherlands pass as one row each with location, error type, E-lines, source, captured stdout and log, the deprecation warning, all 11 short-summary lines with outcome/test/count/reason, and the 2/6/2/1/1/0.11s totals; the intermediate test_pricing.py:29 frame stays inside the source cell rather than its own column, but nothing is lost.
All 80 AST lines become one row each with depth, ancestor path, field, node type and leaf value, so the whole tree is preserved and can be rebuilt.

All six frames (file/line/function/code, tagged by traceback 1-3) and the three exceptions with their chain wording are right, but the SettingsError's two-line message is split: its second line 'source: /etc/orders/worker.json' is filed as a fourth exception row with 'source' as the exception type instead of staying in the SettingsError message.

All 64 opcodes land one per row with offset, code byte, opcode name and argument in stable columns (MEMOIZE/MARK annotations and the non-ASCII strings intact), and the 'highest protocol = 4' summary is kept; only the indentation, which is derivable from the MARK/APPENDS/SETITEMS sequence, is dropped.
All 14 classes (name, bases, line) and all 71 methods (parent class, name, line) are filed in two correctly named datasets, with every method tied to its class and every line number right.

All 8 warnings land one per row with file, line, category, message and the source line from the line below kept in the same record; the two 'Enable tracemalloc' hints are kept in a notes dataset, which can be matched back to their warnings by their unique categories.

All 8 entries sit under the input's own File_Name/Modified/Size header, with names containing spaces and non-ASCII bytes kept whole and the overlong name that breaks column alignment still parsed correctly.

All five sections survive with correct columns: 16 progress lines (percent/type/key/size/unit), 5 biggest-per-type rows, sampled 607 keys, total key length 9380 with avg 15.45, and 6 per-type totals with count/size/unit/percent/avg; the comment banner is kept in notes.

All 9 samples land under the real header names (keys/mem/clients/blocked/requests/connections) with the unlabelled last column sensibly named from its 'child' group and the SAVE flags on the right rows; the requests delta stays in the same cell as the total, which keeps it intact.

All 70 instructions (pos/insn/operands/line/events), the 5 local-table headers and the 10 locals are present and correctly columned, but the six '== disasm: #<ISeq:...>' headers are not applied: the iseq column is empty in every dataset and the headers sit only as 'unread' notes, so nothing says which method/block each instruction or local belongs to (and the [CcCr] event flags stay glued to the operands instead of the events column).
Speed/rows/columns/line and all 17 control characters (including min/time) are filed as named fields, and all 53 mode flags land one per row with their on/off state decoded from the leading minus.
All 44 syscalls across the 8 groups land one per row, each carrying its @group and that group's description comment.

Every section survives: the 7 entries (type, path, target), the '7 overridden configuration files found' summary, the ssh.service diff's ---/+++ file headers with timestamps, the @@ hunk header, and all 8 diff lines with their +/- markers.

All 61 option lines are kept as option/value pairs: the 3 @-prefixed user options are in one dataset and the 58 built-ins in another, values are byte-exact (quotes, array indices and the long status-format strings included), and joining the rows back reproduces the input exactly.

Everything survives with sound structure: PID/version/command and the 3-errors/4-suppressed summary in one row, the three thread announcements, the stats_lock observation, all three races as one row each with access/size/address/thread/locks and the conflicting access plus data-symbol description, all 44 stack frames tagged by context, the program's own 'total=29874 last=2999' line, and the banner/advice lines kept as notes.

All 25 timing lines land one per row with clock and description intact and the 7 sourcing lines correctly split into self+sourced/self, but the second legend line ('clock elapsed: other lines') is not applied: the 18 non-sourcing lines have their elapsed time filed under 'self' (e.g. 'sourcing vimrc file(s)' 024.506 and 'opening buffers' 004.061, which include nested sourcing), so the self column mixes two different measures with nothing marking which is which.

The document properties (version, encoding, URL, standalone) are one row, all 40 tree nodes each sit in their own row with type, name, depth, compact flag, XPath-style path and exact content (whitespace-only text nodes preserved), and the ns namespace declaration is in its own dataset; nothing is lost.

All 105 non-blank lines are kept with the right offset, field, hex value and decoded text, but the synthesized Record column switches from 'LOCAL HEADER #n' to bogus records 'CRC', 'UID' and 'GID' partway through each header, so 75 of 105 rows (filenames and payloads included) are attributed to the wrong record, and 'GID Size' gets Parent 'UID' while UID/GID lose their 'Extra ID #0002' parent.
All 15 error-log entries are kept under the real header names (IDENTIFIER, TIMESTAMP, T, C, RESOURCE_NAME, DESCRIPTION), and the multi-word descriptions are intact in one column.

24 of the 25 attributes land correctly as attribute/value/description/user_settable (the empty location value included), but for unique_id the value is blank and the 48-character id '33213600507680181840a38000000000000E104214503IBMfcp' is merged into the description, because it runs into that column with no gap.
All 45 key/value lines become one record with 45 correctly named columns (END APC becomes END_APC), and every value is intact, units kept and only trailing whitespace trimmed.

All 16 MAC entries land under Vlan/Mac_Address/Type/Ports with correct values, the 'Total Mac Addresses for this criterion: 16' summary is kept as a field/value row, and only the prompt and title banner go to notes.

The CPU-utilization line is kept as one row with five_seconds 38%, interrupt 14%, one_minute 31% and five_minutes 28%, and all 18 processes sit under their real header names with multi-word process names intact; only the prompts go to notes.

Every section survives: the pool status kv (9 fields), 7 pool ServerSide traffic stats, 5 members with availability/state/reason/monitor/status, and 30 member traffic stats with the ServerSide/General columns aligned correctly (Total Requests under General), each keyed by pool and member; only section labels and the prompt go to notes.

All 12 fields are parsed into domain/type/charset/nullability/default/computed-by columns with the continuation CHECK and COLLATE lines attached to SKU and DESCRIPTION, plus all 5 constraints (type, columns, definition) and all 4 triggers (sequence, type, active state).

Every line is accounted for: runner version/revision/name/token/system ID, 8 sections with start/end timestamps and titles, 35 log lines each tagged with its section and command/output kind, and the Job succeeded result; ANSI/CR noise was cleaned.

Both controllers (model, slot, embedded note, serial), 2 drive cages, 4 ports, 4 arrays, 4 logical drives, 18 physical drives (port/box/bay/type/size/status, the spare flag kept, Unassigned drives labelled) and the SEP enclosure (vendor, model, 380, WWID) are all kept, each keyed by controller slot and array.

All 9 disks land under the real ioscan header names, with each disk's continuation device-file lines folded into the same row as Block_Device and Raw_Device lists (including all four slice files for disk 0), so no record is split across rows.

Schedd name/address/time, all 7 batch rows under the real header (including multi-word batch names and the 4103001.0 ... 4104502.0 job range), and both totals lines with every count are filed correctly.

All 20 interfaces are correct under the real header names and the legend is kept, but the legend keys '*down' and '^down' are turned into 'down' and 'down_2', so the '*'/'^' markers that tell you which meaning applies are gone, and the indentation that shows which XGigabitEthernet ports belong to Eth-Trunk10/20 is lost with no parent-trunk column.

The screen header and all 12 status kv pairs (CPU, DB capability, elapsed time, jobs, ASP size/used/total, unprotect, perm/temp addresses) form one row, and all 6 pools sit under correctly merged two-line headers (DB_Fault, Non-DB_Pages, Act-Wait and so on), with the '+++++' value kept; the prompt and F-key lines go to notes.

The server banner, 8 dbspaces (both flags columns), 11 chunks, the counts, the expanded-chunk setting and the NOTE are all present, but chunk 9's 'Metadata 77451 57226 77451' continuation line is split into a separate dataset with no chunk id, and the two 'N active, M maximum' summaries are filed with no column saying which belongs to Dbspaces and which to Chunks.

All five sections survive with their real headers and every value under the right column: model row, 5 apps (blank vault version kept empty), 7 units with leader asterisks and blank ports, 8 machines and 2 offers.

All 38 interface/address lines are kept under Interface/Admin/Link/Proto/Local/Remote, with the interface, admin and link status filled down onto continuation inet6/multiservice address lines and the '-->' targets (ae0.0, 0/0, ::/0) placed in Remote; only the prompts, the header and {master:0} go to notes.

All 22 klog events land one per row with severity, date, time, pid, file, line, message and structured attributes in stable columns, and the multi-line \"Unhandled Error\" record (err=< ... > logger) is kept together in one row.

All three tables survive with their real headers and every row correct (4 instance groups, 5 nodes, 4 validation errors with messages intact), the context/cluster/Error lines become a one-row kv dataset, and the \"Validation Failed\" verdict and section titles are kept in notes.

All 35 taxa are present with percent, clade reads, taxon reads, rank code, taxid and name correctly placed, but the name indentation that encodes tree depth is stripped with no depth column (so e.g. Viruses, a direct child of root, is indistinguishable from Bacteria/Archaea under cellular organisms), and two always-empty Minimizers columns are added.

All 37 key/value pairs land in one wide row under their own key names with values intact (including the composite size strings and the APFS block), and the \"This disk is an APFS Volume\" sub-heading is kept in notes.

All 22 registry nodes land one per row with name, location, class, id, state flags, busy count/time and retain correctly split, but the +-o tree nesting is dropped entirely (no depth or parent column), so which device or interface hangs under which hub/controller can no longer be told from the data.

All 39 scalar attributes land in one record under their names and both parenthesised lists (ContentTypeTree, ScreenCaptureGlobalRect) are kept as attribute/value rows, but the empty kMDItemUserTags = () attribute vanishes entirely and _kMDItemDisplayNameWithExtensions loses its leading underscore in its column name.

All four sections survive with every record correctly split: 9 device types (name/identifier), 4 runtimes (name/version/build/identifier), 13 devices carrying their runtime group and availability down with UDID, state and the unavailable note, and 2 device pairs with their Watch and Phone sub-lines folded into one row each.

All 12 interfaces land one per row with index, flags, ;;; comment and every key=value (including continuation-line link times and link-downs) under its own key name, absent keys left blank, and the prompt and Flags legend kept in notes.

All 12 sessions land under the real sp_who2 headers with multi-word values (Command, ProgramName, LastBatch) intact, HostName/BlkBy '.' and the blocking SPID 62 correctly placed, and both REQUESTID rows of SPID 62 kept; only the trailing duplicate SPID column, identical in every row, and the dash rule are dropped.

All 10 two-line sessions are kept together one per row, with the two-line header applied and the src/dst address strings decomposed into IP, port, zone, proto, vsys and translated IP/port columns, every value checked in place and blank flags left blank.

The single UNPAIRED metrics row lands under all 35 real Picard column names with every value in place (trailing empty SAMPLE/LIBRARY/READ_GROUP kept blank), and the ## header, command line, Started-on timestamp and METRICS CLASS lines are kept verbatim in notes.

All 38 lines are accounted for and the Started/Processing/Completed/other events are well parsed into named columns (method, path, IP, controller#action, status, Views/ActiveRecord/Allocations with absent timings left blank), but the two FATAL events are split: their rows in log_entries have an empty Message while the exception text (RecordNotFound, RoutingError) and the backtrace sit as 7 separate rows, including blank ones, in a continuation_lines dataset linked only by Request_ID.
All 9 hosts (including the global pseudo-host and the dashes of the down host cn-0103) land one per row under the 11 real header names with every value in its column; only the rule line was dropped.

Every section survives with real headers and values in place: the database row (multi-word status intact), 4 device fragments (dates and \"not applicable\" kept whole), the log-only free kbytes total as kv, and 5 device/segment rows, with the (1 row affected) and (return status = 0) summary lines kept in notes.

All 43 lines land one per row across four datasets with time/status/block kept: the 15 test service messages are parsed into name/duration/message/flowId, the 4 step headers into step/total/name/duration, and the block and build lines keep their full text (the buildStatisticValue, testStdOut and publishArtifacts messages stay as raw text in block_log rather than parsed, but nothing is lost or misplaced).

No dataset was filed: provost held the capture in 'unsorted' (kv-pairs coverage 50%, LLM template declined), so none of the 9 pipe-separated client records or the error id=0 msg=ok status line was extracted.

All 9 result rows land under the real column names with multi-word and UTF-8 store names whole, null timestamps kept as \"?\" and the negative amount intact, while the banner/release/charset/RC become a session row, the SELECT with its 9 rows/4 columns/1 second summary a query row, and the logon/logoff/elapsed lines are kept in notes.

All four BCD entries are kept, one row each with entry_type and every key as a named column holding the right value, and the three-line displayorder list is joined into one cell; the only oddity is that the third boot loader (different key set) went to a separate Windows_Boot_Loader.v2 dataset rather than alongside the other two, with nothing lost.

Every section of both the computer and user halves survives with a Scope column: the header kv (created-on, RSOP user/computer/mode, OS, profiles) as one summary row, the two settings blocks with DN, 7 applied GPOs, 5 filtered GPOs with their Filtering reason and WMI filter kept with the GPO, and all 23 security groups, with banner and section titles in notes.

All 7 sessions land as one row each under the real header names (USERNAME, SESSIONNAME, ID, STATE, IDLE_TIME, LOGON_TIME), blank session names stay empty rather than shifting columns, the '>' current-session marker is kept in its own column, and the multibyte username line is parsed correctly.

All sections survive and are correctly shaped: job header (Started/Source/Dest/Files/Options), 7 directory lines with status and counts, 9 files tagged with their parent directory, 3 ERROR 32 retry events one row each (the final RETRY LIMIT EXCEEDED folded into the third), the Dirs/Files/Bytes/Times summary with the sparse Times row correctly aligned under Total/Copied/FAILED/Extras, and the speed/Ended totals; only the banner went to notes.

All 4 task blocks become one row each with all 28 keys as named columns plus the Folder heading carried onto each task (\\\\Fabrikam for three, \\\\Fabrikam\\\\Wartung for the last); every value, including the empty Power Management, the multi-part Repeat keys and the trailing-$ Task To Run, sits under the right column.

All 21 processes land one per row under the 9 real header names, with multi-word image names, user names and window titles (including the non-ASCII and en-dash titles) kept whole, 'Not Responding' intact in Status, and the separator rule dropped as decoration.

All 25 privileges land one per row under the real headers Privilege_Name/Description/State with multi-word descriptions intact and Enabled/Disabled correct; only the title and the header line itself went to notes.

All 10 connections land under the 21 #fields names with every value in its correct column (including -, (empty), IPv6 addresses, comma sets and tunnel_parents), and the separator/set_separator/empty_field/unset_field/path/open/close directives form a metadata row; the #fields and #types lines are kept verbatim in notes.

The four catalog entries come out as tidy entry_type/entry_name/section/key/value rows with every key-value present (the ATTRIBUTES flags and the SYSTEM-TIMESTAMP value that wraps onto the next line are kept), along with the 14-row ENTRIES PROCESSED counts and both IDC messages; but the cluster's PROTECTION-PSWD and RACF values are tagged with section SMSDATA when they are a separate group, and the numeric summary THE NUMBER OF PROTECTED ENTRIES SUPPRESSED WAS 1 is only kept as unparsed skipped text in notes.
